transport: TLS 1.3 mTLS originator-binding front (Node https, child process) -> loopback HTTP -> actual Mobius4; TLS 1.3 mTLS Mosquitto (CN ACL, mount_point) -> originator guard -> Mobius4 MQTT binding

pki.generator: openssl (run-local throwaway CA under .local, deleted with the run directory)

bindingModel.identity: SAN URI (urn:privacy-bubble:acp-mtls:<role>) with SHA-256 certificate pin; CN used as MQTT username
bindingModel.originatorRule: one certificate identity -> exactly one AE originator; AE-ID pre-assigned and registered by the certificate holder
bindingModel.mismatch: HTTP 403 + X-M2M-RSC 4103 + pb:originatorBinding.code, request never forwarded
bindingModel.revocation: remove the row from the binding table; the front re-reads the file per request (stat key) without restart
bindingModel.auditPrivacy: originators logged as domain-separated SHA-256 digests (16 hex), request bodies as SHA-256 only, no payload content

listeners.external: loopback TLS 1.3, require_certificate, use_identity_as_username, mount_point ext/, generated ACL

real: Mosquitto broker process with TLS 1.3 and ACL
notCovered: Raspberry Pi Gateway and keyring hardware
nginx front (template only, nginx is not installed on this host)
CSE-to-AE notification delivery over TLS (loopback HTTP receiver)
Mosquitto ACL reload on revocation (the guard enforces revocation live; the ACL file is regenerated on restart)
direct loopback access to the CSE HTTP port by other local processes (deployment keeps that port on a private network or socket)
CRL or OCSP revocation of certificates (revocation acts on the binding table)
